And in this year a great force of the Slavs, that is to say the Russians, came against the imperial city by sea and by land.
And God helped the Romans,
and they cast fire and burned their ships in the sea;
and most of them were burned and drowned.
And they likewise captured many of those who came by land,
and cut off their right hands;
and there was a great victory for the Romans.
And at this time, when foreigners—Armenians, Arabs, and Jews—had multiplied in the imperial city,
a riot arose in it against the emperor Constantine.
And the peoples gathered at the palace gate and were shouting:
"Behold, Constantine has killed both our empresses!"
And they were seeking a pretext
to plunder the palace and the mansions of the grandees.
Then the emperor Constantine assembled the magnates,
and brought out Theodora and Zoe, adorned in imperial attire.
And when the rioters saw them,
they grew quiet.
Now the emperor, when he investigated the cause of the riot, was told:
"The foreigners caused it in order to plunder the city."
Then the emperor commanded
that no one who had entered it within the last thirty years should remain in it.
And whoever stayed
would have his eyes gouged out.
Then about one hundred thousand souls went out.
And in the year 436
[436] of the Arabs,
an envoy was sent by al-Qa'im the Caliph to Toghril Beg;
and his embassy was based upon four points.
The first point:
The Commander of the Faithful says to you,
"O Amir Toghril Beg Muhammad,
the lands that you have taken are sufficient for you,
and do not be covetous (or: do not make yourself strong) any further over the lands of the rest of the Arab rulers,
and do not ruin them."
And the second:
"That you submit to our obedience,
and swear to us canonical oaths with the divorce of your lawful wives, the manumission of your slaves, and the almsgiving (or: scattering)"
